clue.text: Speculate about the way a woman reads the newspaper

indicators.note: about means the bet is placed around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to speculate is to bet
a road is a way
she stands for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone muses on how a lady reads her paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A broadsheet is the large-format paper, long the sign of the serious British press.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a large-format paper, traditionally the serious press.

clue.text: Gold backing of covering

indicators.note: backing in a down clue tells us the word for gold is written backwards

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold backing used as the lining of a covering.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'backing' reads the gold word upwards; OR for gold comes from heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof is the covering on top of a building.

clue.text: The guidance of a daughter over some fault

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first pieces above the next one

parts.note: a vice is a fault of character

explanation.surface: A girl offers guidance about a failing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' sets A and D on top of VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is counsel or guidance offered to someone.

clue.text: Miser-a fool accepting credit with hesitation

indicators.note: accepting means the word for fool takes the credit abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A stingy person is called a fool for hesitantly accepting credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miser-a' joins definition to wordplay with a hyphen; 'accepting' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A scraper is a skinflint who scrapes together every penny.

clue.text: This country needs some much bolder investors

indicators.note: some says only part of the letters of the following words are wanted

explanation.surface: A nation needs braver people to put money in.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across bolDER INvestors.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is the old poetic name for Ireland.

clue.text: Nails glisten, given special treatment

annotationWithheld.why: 'Nails glisten, given special treatment' as held: 'glisten' is the anagram fodder for TINGLES but 'Nails' does not define tingles; the definition word looks misread and no source gives the printed clue.

clue.text: The union encompassing exemplary fidelity

indicators.note: encompassing means the union word wraps round the abbreviation for example

parts.note: an alliance is a union
EG, for example, is suggested by exemplary

explanation.surface: A marriage that contains model loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encompassing' is the container signal; 'exemplary' hints at the Latin abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is loyalty owed to a ruler or cause.

clue.text: Ruling for the odd ten-man game

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: Unusual governance for a peculiar team game with ten players.
explanation.definitionFit: Management is the act of running or controlling an organisation.

clue.text: Seaweed left in a state

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left within the other letters

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Seaweed abandoned somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: An alga is a simple water plant; seaweeds are large examples.

clue.text: Getting a number on account makes a change

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a version is an account of events

explanation.surface: Getting a figure credited to an account alters things.
explanation.walkthrough: Any Roman numeral can stand for 'a number'; here C (100).
explanation.definitionFit: A conversion is a transformation from one form to another.

clue.text: A green alternative of sorts

indicators.note: alternative suggests another arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Environmentally friendly choices of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are biological categories, kinds or types.

clue.text: He could well drive one round the bend!

definitions.text: He could well drive one round the bend!

parts.words: He could well drive one round the bend!
parts.note: driving someone round the bend sounds like maddening them, but literally it is guiding a vehicle along a curve

explanation.surface: An annoying person who drives others mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A steerer is someone who guides a vehicle's direction.

clue.text: Turnover resulting from personal endeavour

parts.note: turnover suggests business revenue earned by effort, but here it is a body turning over by its own effort

explanation.surface: Business revenue earned by one's own hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A somersault is a flip in which a person turns heels over head under their own power.

clue.text: People entitled to cultivate an area of London

parts.note: earls are people with titles
to court is to cultivate someone's favour

explanation.surface: Nobles set out to develop a part of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Earls Court is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls Court is a named district in the west of the capital.

clue.text: Taking river fish, anglers require such equipment

parts.note: eels are fish

explanation.surface: Fishermen need the right gear to land a catch from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Reels are the winding devices fishing rods carry for line.

clue.text: Dicky said look around by the water

indicators.note: around means the word for look goes round the shuffled letters

parts.note: to see is to look

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky told someone to look about at the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a man's name but is British slang for shaky, the anagram signal; 'around' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside place is one on the coast beside the sea.

clue.text: Dawn finds a French male in drink

indicators.note: in says the French article goes inside the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
un is the French for a with a masculine noun

explanation.surface: At daybreak a Frenchman is found drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'a French male' wants the masculine French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is the moment of sunrise, the start of daylight.

clue.text: A problem concerning public transport

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: An issue regarding buses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures stand for words.

clue.text: An evangelist making an impression

explanation.surface: A preacher who leaves a lasting effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark is one of the four Gospel writers, and a mark is a trace or impression left on something.

clue.text: Formerly an essential part of coronation ceremony

indicators.note: an essential part of says the answer is a run of letters held inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: In the past, something central to crowning a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Formerly an essential' is not a phrase meaning the answer; 'Formerly' alone defines it and 'an essential part of' is the indicator. The run is coronatiON CEremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past.

clue.text: Dull, cold, and vulgar

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
loud means garish or vulgar

explanation.surface: A description of a boring, chilly and coarse person.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloud something is to dull or obscure it.

clue.text: A cretin-really stupid without a doubt

indicators.note: really stupid suggests the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: A very foolish idiot is absolutely sure.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain means sure, free of doubt.

clue.text: The medical attendant has a duty to ensure dryness

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
ought means has a duty to

explanation.surface: A doctor must make sure patients stay dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long period without rain.

clue.text: Desires break, but stays

indicators.note: break means the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wants fall apart, yet someone remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live or stay in a place.

clue.text: Object when moulder cuts a troublesome person

indicators.note: cuts means the decay word slices into the nuisance word

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance
to rot is to moulder

explanation.surface: Complaining when decay hits an annoying individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moulder' looks like someone who moulds, but it is the verb to decay; 'cuts' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to raise an objection.

clue.text: An individual who minds being sensitive

explanation.surface: Someone who cares for others is touchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender looks after something, like a bartender, and tender means sore or easily hurt.

clue.text: The sum a horse will fetch

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: The price a horse will sell for.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a total or quantity.

clue.text: Sticks around, plainly self-satisfied

indicators.note: around means the word for sticks is turned the other way

parts.note: to gum is to stick

explanation.surface: Someone who stays close, obviously pleased with himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug means complacent and pleased with oneself.

clue.text: A child's sums

explanation.surface: Arithmetic done by a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading needs the apostrophe: a tot's, belonging to a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, and to tot up is to add figures, so tots are sums.

clue.text: Dreadful conflict of a member with elderly fellow

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
aged means elderly
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A terrible war involving a limb and an old academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the final great battle, any catastrophic war.

clue.text: A game bird

explanation.surface: A bit of fun with a feathered creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a prank or bit of fun, and also a songbird such as the skylark.

clue.text: No retiring man would wear such a thing!

definitions.text: No retiring man would wear such a thing!

parts.words: No retiring man would wear such a thing!
parts.note: retiring sounds like shy, but here it means going to bed, and the garment is one worn by women at bedtime

explanation.surface: A shy fellow would never wear something so showy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a woman's loose gown worn for sleeping.
